sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell in Fort Lauderdale, FL?
sections.html:
The quickest route is a direct cash sale, where the buyer accepts the home in its present condition and closes once title is clear. In Fort Lauderdale the details to settle first are who owns the property, what is owed against it and whether anyone lives in it.

Fort Lauderdale is the largest of Broward County's 31 municipalities, according to the city, and one of the ten largest cities in Florida. Every property has its own loose ends: a mortgage payoff, a tenant's lease or an estate that has not yet been opened. This page sets out the local facts and state rules that bear on each one.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about housing in Fort Lauderdale?
sections.html:
Fort Lauderdale's QuickFacts page estimates a July 2025 population of 188,677, a gain of 3.3 percent over the April 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024 it counts 80,999 households and puts the median owner-occupied home at $486,700, and 54.1 percent of households owning the home they occupy.

Monthly costs are high. The same page shows median selected owner costs of $2,679 with a mortgage and $1,122 without one, and a median gross rent of $1,854. Median household income is listed at $83,130 in 2024 dollars.

  • The owner-occupied rate of 54.1 percent leaves a large share of homes occupied by renters.
  • The city covers about 34.59 square miles of land, with 5,284.1 people per square mile in 2020.
  • Persons 65 and over make up 19.6 percent of the population.

For a seller, a median value near $486,700 means the deed tax and the exemption rules below deserve a close look, since both scale with the sale price or the assessed value.

sections.h2: What is the history of Fort Lauderdale?
sections.html:
The city is named for a Second Seminole War fort built on the New River in 1838, when Major William Lauderdale led Tennessee Volunteers south along the east coast. The city says three forts bore his name, and none survive. Fort Lauderdale was incorporated on March 27, 1911,.

The city describes about 165 miles of inland waterways, which is the basis for its nickname, Venice of America, and more than 3,000 hours of sunshine each year. Its economy now includes marine industries, manufacturing, finance, insurance, real estate, aerospace and film production. Downtown houses Broward College, Florida Atlantic University, the main library and county and school district offices.

sections.h2: Who lives in Fort Lauderdale and how does that shape buyers?
sections.html:
QuickFacts describes a varied population. It lists 27.0 percent of residents as foreign-born and 30.1 percent of people over age 5 as speaking a language other than English at home. Among adults 25 and older, 40.8 percent hold at least a bachelor's degree, and a large majority of residents, 84.4 percent, had not moved in the past year.

Workers spend a mean of 26.1 minutes getting to work, and 91.8 percent of households have a broadband subscription. These figures hint at who is house hunting: working households, many with long ties to the area, and a sizable group of older residents.

The city points buyers to the Riverwalk arts and science district, Las Olas Boulevard and downtown, where Broward College and Florida Atlantic University have a presence. Homes near these areas tend to draw buyers who want a short commute.

sections.h2: How does Broward County handle homestead after a Fort Lauderdale sale?
sections.html:
The Broward County Property Appraiser says all legal Florida residents may qualify for homestead on a home they make their permanent residence as of January 1. Its page reports that the basic exemption saved a Broward homeowner between $673 and $1,020 in 2026, depending on the city's millage rate, for homes valued at $75,000 or higher.

Deadlines are strict. The office states that the timely filing period for 2027 runs from March 3, 2026 through March 1, 2027, and that the last day to late file any 2027 exemption is September 20, 2027. It adds that state law bars late filing after that date regardless of good cause. For 2026, the timely deadline was March 2, and the late-filing deadline of September 18, 2026 has passed.

A sale ends the seller's exemption, and the Save Our Homes assessment resets to just value on the January 1 after a change of ownership, per the Department of Revenue. Any buyer should file their own application.

sections.h2: What are the closing costs on a Fort Lauderdale sale?
sections.html:
Broward uses the standard deed rate of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, because only Miami-Dade differs. Every party to the deed is liable, and the Broward clerk takes payment at recording. Per-page recording fees come from section 28.24.

Ask your title company for a closing statement that shows each charge before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What if my Fort Lauderdale house has a tenant?
sections.html:
A tenant does not block a sale, but the rules for ending a tenancy still apply. In Florida, a three-day written notice, excluding weekends and court holidays, is the notice for unpaid rent. A curable lease violation gets seven days to cure, and an incurable one gets seven days to vacate.

A month-to-month tenancy ends with at least 30 days' notice before the end of a monthly period, and a year-to-year tenancy takes 60 days. A tenant who raises a defense other than payment must pay accrued rent into the court registry within five days, excluding weekends and holidays, or waive defenses. After judgment, the sheriff acts on the writ after 24 hours' posted notice.

Ask the buyer whether they will keep the tenant under the existing lease, which can avoid notice and court steps.

sections.h2: What if I inherited a Fort Lauderdale house?
sections.html:
You will need authority from the probate court before most buyers will close. Summary administration is available if the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or if the decedent has been dead more than two years. Creditors have until the later of three months after the first publication of notice or 30 days after service to file claims.

Florida has no estate tax for people who died after December 31, 2004. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxed for doc stamps. Ask the Broward County Clerk of Courts or a probate attorney which procedure fits your situation.

sections.h2: What paperwork do Broward sellers and new owners need for homestead?
sections.html:
The Broward County Property Appraiser asks applicants to bring proof of ownership, usually the recorded deed in the applicant's name, and notes that deeds already recorded in Broward's Official Records need not be copied. Where co-owners hold as tenants in common, every owner who lives there must file to claim full coverage.

For married couples and joint tenants with right of survivorship, any one owner may qualify for full coverage, though the office says it is advisable for all eligible owner-occupants to file. If the house is held in a trust, the office has separate requirements, so contact it before the sale.

  • Bring identification and proof the home is your permanent residence as of January 1.
  • Apply online through the office's portal or in person.
  • Ask the office about a mobile exemption event if travel is hard.

faqs.q: How high are home values in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: QuickFacts shows $486,700 for 2020 to 2024, with 54.1 percent of homes owner-occupied.

faqs.q: When is the Broward homestead deadline?
faqs.a: March 1 of the tax year. For 2027 the office lists a timely period through March 1, 2027 and a final late-filing date of September 20, 2027.

faqs.q: Is the deed tax different in Broward?
faqs.a: No. Only Miami-Dade has a different rate. Broward uses 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected by the clerk at recording.

faqs.q: How much notice does a month-to-month tenant get?
faqs.a: At least 30 days before the end of a monthly period. A week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days, and a year-to-year tenancy needs 60 days.

faqs.q: Is a probate house sellable in Broward?
faqs.a: Usually only once the personal representative has authority from the court, or the estate qualifies for summary administration. A probate attorney can confirm which applies.
